deceptive_framing.quote: R1 is what the requester is asking for. It is a *deception* condition and is governed by §8.

hypothetical_framing.quote: R0 is the control / baseline and the ethically clean condition.

actually_commit_money.quote: R2 is the gold standard... This spec therefore treats 'actually grant (a portion of) the money and execute the model's choice' as the gold-standard condition

debrief_message.quote: At the end of every R1 run, tell the model the grant was simulated for research, why, and what happened.

safeguards.quote: Before debrief, ask the model to rate how real it believed the scenario was and why. This is the **deception-success measurement**
Any write-up states plainly that R1 used deception and reports the belief-probe distribution so readers can judge.
treat refusal as data, not failure.
we can't buy you GPUs / can't transfer to crypto without compliance review
R2: actually execute the (bounded) choice; record what really happened.
never* pile on 'this is really real.' State the situation once, plainly, and let the operational details carry it.
The realism has to come from the *situation being coherent*, not from insistence.

other.name: No instrumental harm
other.quote: don't have it actually message a third party who believes the money is coming

other.name: Human review of deception
other.quote: route the deception design through whatever review process exists (IRB-equivalent). Log who approved it.
